name: Ethiopia
summary_text: Ethiopia is dangerous for trans visitors. Same-sex activity is criminalised (up to 1 year, or more under aggravating provisions), and because Ethiopia has no legal gender recognition, trans people are legally treated as their birth sex — meaning a trans person's ordinary relationships can be prosecuted as same-sex conduct. The 2024 UPR stakeholder report documents discrimination, violence, and absence of police protection, with trans women and queer women particularly at risk, plus a growing organised anti-LGBTQ+ campaign inside the country. Documented trans-specific enforcement is thinner than Cameroon's or Tunisia's — Ethiopia's LGBTQ+ community (self-identified as “zega”) is deeply underground, and reporting is sparse — but the legal structure (criminalisation + no LGR catch-all), hostile campaigning, and absence of any protection place it clearly on the dangerous side of the scale. Digital surveillance and blackmail vulnerability are noted in the UPR reporting.

sources.claim_summary: Stakeholder submission to Ethiopia's UPR (47th session): same-sex activity criminalised, leaving LGBTQ+ people at serious risk of harm and systematic exclusion; discrimination, violence, lack of police protection and stigma in services; no legal gender change - trans men are legally women and trans women legally men, so trans people in different-gender relationships can fall foul of the same-sex conduct law.

Stakeholder UPR report by The Advocates for Human Rights and House of Guramayle (April 2024) on SOGIE in Ethiopia: documents discrimination, violence, and lack of protection; notes transgender people are particularly at risk given the criminalisation framework.

sources.title: Ethiopia - F&M Global Barometers
sources.claim_summary: F&M Global Barometers country profile for Ethiopia: composite LGBT-rights perception scores including the Global Barometer of Transgender Rights index.
US State Department 2008 Human Rights Report for Ethiopia (archived): documents the criminalisation of same-sex conduct and societal stigma - baseline country-of-origin information.

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Ethiopia (archived): documents arrests of opposition figures, CSO-law restrictions on civil society, and the LGBT section noting criminalisation and societal discrimination.

US State Department 2010 Human Rights Report for Ethiopia: documents the anti-terrorism prosecutions, CSO-law restrictions, torture, harsh prisons - general context with the LGBT section noting criminalisation.

Lund University master's thesis (2009) by Daniel Iddo Balcha: 'Homosexuality in Ethiopia' - analyses the construction of homosexuality in relation to gender and feminism; male homosexuality criminalised (up to 3 years); media and elite create homophobia in discourse; the church effectively campaigns hatred; female homosexuality simply overlooked; attitudes shifting under globalisation.
